A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SwiftKV. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-quality, throughput, latency, distillation, compression, and early-exit experiments in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds model evaluations and a memory-budget comparison in Table 5 and Appendix B.3.

M1.justification: SingleInputKV, AcrossKV, QKV-only distillation, and the optimized vLLM inference procedure remain unchanged. The early-exit extension is retained in the appendices. Additional model evaluations and the redrawn architecture diagram do not document a changed SwiftKV procedure.

E1.justification: The training corpora, benchmark tasks, math/code data ablation, Alpaca examples, and batch/interactive inference workloads are retained. Additions vary model configurations and available GPU memory within these tasks, without introducing different datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 introduces Merge-all-Layers, an idealized zero-overhead cache-compression comparator, in Section 5.1/Table 5. Existing comparisons are retained. Newly discussed ALISA and MInference are cited as related work but are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands model configurations to Llama-3.2-3B, FP8/W8A8 Llama-3.1-405B, Mistral-Small-Instruct-2409, and DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, including 40% and 45% prefill-reduction settings. Table 5 adds H100 memory limits of 80, 40, 20, and 16 GB. Settings for the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.1 adds a focused analysis of compute reduction versus cache compression under varying memory budgets. Additional model evaluations examine compression sensitivity, particularly 40% versus 50% skipping for the 3B model and two-way versus four-way sharing for DeepSeek. Earlier ablations and early-exit studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-to-run error bars. Point-estimate reporting and the existing early-exit probability analysis are retained.

E6.justification: Retained numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results for four models and the memory-budget study. For example, Table B.3 reports FP8 405B averages of 86.6 for the baseline and 85.9 with 50% SingleInputKV. Table 5 newly reports throughput and out-of-memory outcomes across memory limits.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix B's symbolic FLOP derivation, including the 24d^2 operation count and KV-cost bound for G >= 4, is removed. v2 provides a model-specific numerical computation breakdown in Table 1 instead. Equations 1–3 and the approximate l/L computation ratio remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add released training/inference code and usable SwiftKV models as a contribution. The central method, compression, quality-preservation, and headline throughput and latency claims retain their original meaning and scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of suitability for moderate-context, MLP-dominated workloads and of compute versus memory bottlenecks. Section 4.2 also qualifies generalization with stricter compression limits for the 3B and DeepSeek models. Existing dataset-quality, training, and early-exit limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports releasing training and inference implementations and ready-to-use SwiftKV models, with an access link in the abstract and introduction. This substantially expands the reproduction resources documented by the paper. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, and vLLM settings are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises positioning toward sparse-attention prefill acceleration through ALISA and MInference, and toward compute-versus-memory bottlenecks. It removes the earlier speculative-decoding/model-distillation comparison and its Medusa, Minitron, and survey citations. DeepSeek-V2 is newly cited for the additional architecture.

P1.justification: Related-work and prefill-computation prose receive targeted rewrites. Full/partial fine-tuning discussion is merged into the distillation subsection, while dataset and early-exit discussions move to Appendices D and E. Most wording and the overall introduction–method–results–conclusion structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to distinguish computed/skipped prefill operations and trainable parameters. New computation, model-summary, memory-budget, and per-model tables substantially expand the visual presentation. Dataset and early-exit displays move into appendices; existing performance plots retain their contents.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens practical validation through additional architectures, explicit compression limits, and a controlled memory-budget study. The clearer diagram and documented code/model access also improve understanding and reproducibility. These are useful extensions of the retained main evidence, partly offset by removing v1's general FLOP derivation.
